| **PROS**    | **CONS**  |
|-------------|-----------|
| **Soft Flask** |
| 🟢 Ease of use and collapsible | 🟡 Only holds 500ml |
| 🟢 Fit any where | 🟡 Can puncture |
| **Cycling Bottle** |
| 🟢 Holds > 1 l | 🟡 Won't stay on deck |
| 🟢 Available | 🟡 Some bite valves terrible |


# Summary
This isn't a review of any particular bottle, since there are so many, but more of a comparison of collapsible or squishy bottles, such as Salomon soft flasks designed for ultra running vests, versus rigid squirt bottles typically found on road bikes or handed out as schwag at running races. My system is the soft flask on the deck or front deck hatch since the bungee holds them down nicely, but 1-2 bottles in my day hatch.

The soft flasks are great since they're compact and stay put, yet they only hold 500 ml, not really enough for a paddle over two hours. I've looked for one-liter soft flasks, but they don't seem to exist. The expectation is you'll just buy two. When I stop, I then refill the soft flask with another bottle. If I'm super thirsty, the larger bottles are still behind me in the day hatch. 

Why not just put the cycling bottles on the front deck? I've lost too many that way. In any kind of surf or rough conditions, if they aren't tied on, they're gone. OK, you could put them on a leash, but as soon as you get mashed by a wave, it's a yard sale, like those backpackers with clanging pots and pans tied on to their packs when you manage to get up again.

What about hydration packs in your buoyancy aid? Those are great, but my [Astral BA](https://3point.xyz/kayak-review/astral-ba/) only has a fake hydration pack sleeve that says 'water,' but nothing fits into it. Maybe it's more of an incantation to the sea for where water should or shouldn't go when it gets rough. But frankly, not having to carry that water on your back while paddling is nice, and there's always room in the boat. I suppose if I were in a long race and needed water by flicking the bite valve to my mouth, I would use a pack with my [Peak BA](https://3point.xyz/kayak-review/peak-ba/).
